sentences.text: This bird possessed a relatively large head.
Its beak was about half the length of the head and expanded from top to bottom.
Fossils show a ring of feathers around the skull, likely forming a crest.
A complete skeleton was first described in 1976 as the species Primobucco olsoni.
The genus name Cyrilavis was established in 2010 to replace Primobucco because the bird was reclassified as a halcyornithid rather than a puffbird relative.
The name honors the paleontologist Cyril Walker.
A second species, Cyrilavis colburnorum, was described in 2011 based on a nearly complete skeleton.
In Cyrilavis, the hand bone is much shorter than the forearm bone, which contrasts with the anatomy of modern parrots.
Cyrilavis belongs to the Halcyornithidae, a group that split before parrots and songbirds diverged, making it equally related to both.
Cyrilavis lived between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian stage.
It inhabited the United States within the Fossil Butte Member of the Green River Formation.
